lines.english: "So according to you, spending yet another day flirting with your husband takes priority over reuniting with your own mother…
"It's not my fault. My body has been thoroughly conditioned to wither away whenever Haruki isn't around."
"Don't put it like that!"
Today was another eventful day, but after a brief meeting with the Japanese branch of our company (Kudou-san), I concluded all my "work" in Japan.
Although, even what I'm doing right now could be considered honorable work, as I'm having dinner with the esteemed president of our company.
Of course, neither the hostess nor our guest seem to see it that way…
"Besides, you never acted like a proper parent when I was a child to begin with. This is no less than your just deserts."
"K-Kazusa… how cold of you. You mean to say that you couldn't care less if your mother died alone in some barren corner of the world?
"You sure did. No doubt about it."
"…Guitar-kun, you're rather cold yourself."
"Besides, we talked over video chat for over five hours the day before departure, didn't we?"
"Oh did we, now?"
"How about you do your job instead, Kazusa…"
In fact, this is no more and no less than a loving family sitting around a dinner table.
These two have always found themselves separated for one reason or another,
"Well, let's set the formalities aside for now, and raise a toast."
"I'd love to hear what part of our conversation just now was 'formal' to you."
"Whenever you're around, Haruki, even the most cheerful family gathering feels like a board meeting."
"If you're going to curse anyone, you should curse yourself for choosing an inflexible control freak instead of enjoying freedom like me."
"Keep talking."
Almost as if trying to make up for the past dissonance between them, they now share a bond that binds them even stronger than when they were living together.
"Hey, by the way, is he still as stiff as ever?"
"How old do you think we are now? He's obviously as stiff as any man could possibly be, every single day."
"Okay, both of you, stop saying things that could be horribly misinterpreted!"
Though to be honest, their bond right now is so powerful that I feel slightly uncomfortable having to sit next to them.
"Another bottle of absurdly expensive alcohol…"
"So what? This is my first one-on-one meeting with my daughter in so long."
The wine Youko-san ordered is a 1989 vintage Chateau Haut-Brion.
I've read about it in a feature article about wine once before. One of those bottles can easily go for at least 100,000 yen.
"Hey, do you remember, Kazusa? This is the same wine we ordered during our first visit to this restaurant."
"Of course I don't remember. You gulped the whole thing down all by yourself."
1989 also happens to be the year of my birth.
…Of course, that's probably not the reason Youko-san chose this exact wine.
"Ah, of course, you were still underage at the time. Oh how I remember seeing you cry your eyes out over your first heartbreak."
"Huh?"
"Say another word and I'm going home. I'm not talking about the hotel, I'm going straight back to Vienna."
And it seems that the actual story surrounding this wine is one I'll never get to hear about.
"W-Well, setting the price aside, you do have permission from your doctor to drink this, right?"
"Indeed, they told me I can drink as long as I do so in moderation. I don't intend on wasting my life either."
"…Speaking of, how are you feeling lately?"
"Well, I'm doing my best. I take regular check-ups and I don't neglect my medication. I'm doing everything the doctors told me to do to the letter."
It's been three years since Youko-san was diagnosed with leukemia.
Just as Youko-san herself said back then, not even tomorrow was a certainty for her.
"At the very least, I can see myself living long enough to name my first grandchild, attend her entrance ceremony, see her reach adulthood,
"No, you'd be a lich at that point. Also, don't kill off our child before the poor thing is even born."
"…Then perhaps you should present me with a grandchild soon so I don't have to become a lich."
"Well, um… I'll think about it."
Whether this conversation bears any greater meaning or not, Kazusa's attitude changes immediately upon hearing it, opting now to eat without uttering a word.
In fact, she's always like this when she talks to Youko-san.
Even when talking to Youko-san over video chat, she refuses to ever touch the subject.
It's not like I don't understand her feelings, if anything, I understand them all too well…
It's just that I really need to know.
Because if the worst were to happen to Youko-san, it'd be my duty to protect Kazusa mentally.
This is the purpose I promised Youko-san I would fulfill.
"In that case… let us share a toast in honor of our new family member who is certain to be conceived any day now. You'll do your part too, won't you Kazusa?"
"I've never been against the idea once. It's only my tightfisted manager who keeps rejecting the idea."
"I just said I'd… um… think about it."
One of the reasons I'm reluctant to have a child with Kazusa… is that I don't want "the birth" to coincide with "the inevitable."
I don't want Kazusa to be forced to bear the burden of losing someone and meeting someone new at the same time.
In the end, Kazusa is all that matters to me… even if that means I have to sacrifice Youko-san's happiness.
But that can also be said about Youko-san…
Youko-san knows that I'm trying to estimate when "the inevitable" will happen.
She knows that I'm preparing myself for the moment she passes the torch to me.
Because… the two of us are close enough to be that frank with each other. We're mother and son now, after all.
"Anyway, about our schedule…"
"You can't be serious. Why would we hold a wedding ceremony so late?"
"Why, because you two haven't actually held a proper ceremony."
It was when dinner was over, when we had finished our drinks and our tongues were thoroughly loosened when it happened.
It was then that Youko-san finally started discussing the real reason for inviting us back to Japan.
"Nowadays plenty of people skip wedding ceremonies."
Yes, it's about Kazusa's and my wedding ceremony.
A celebratory ceremony that the two of us, having run away from Japan and betrayed everything we had, could never be allowed to hold.
"That won't do. You still haven't given your beloved mother her bouquet yet."
"You're the only mother who would pester her daughter about that."
"You know, hearing you say 'Mom, thank you for everything' all teary-eyed while reading your wedding letter is the reason I'm trying to live a long life."
"Why does your love always have to be so twisted…?"
Ever since we arrived in Vienna, we've lived our lives with our backs turned to the people we used to love.
The first sign of that snow beginning to melt was about half a year ago.
It came in the form of a visit to Vienna by Youko-san, who took the trip despite her illness.
"You two should begin to resolve yourselves… You came back to Japan knowing this was the purpose, didn't you?"
Yes, we knew. None of this is coming out of the blue.
True, Youko-san did force the issue a bit, but we were the ones who consented in the end.
The guilt from being in the same place as those we made unhappy. The shame of showing our faces once more. The memories of our horrible last farewells.
The pain associated with returning to Japan still remains strong within us.
The joy of being in the same place as those we once loved. The adoration we feel for the country we were raised in.
In the same way, these naive hopes also remain deep within us.
"The time and place are still secret for now… I'll tell you when it happens."
Without a doubt, this is an absurd plan we're going along with.
But even then, we find ourselves unable to question Youko-san's scheming, left only to gawk at her self-assured expression.
"Until that time comes, go out there and enjoy your dear Japan… How about catching up with some old friends?"
